name: SPAR Österreich
desc: Austrian family-owned grocery retailer operating SPAR, Interspar and Maximarkt stores plus shopping centres in Central Europe.
capacity_detail: Group revenue EUR 23.3bn including foreign operations (2025 data); about USD 25.6bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Grocery retail in Austria, Italy, Slovenia, Hungary and Croatia, plus SES shopping centres.
rationale: Major Central European grocer with strong Austrian brand could use F1's Red Bull Ring audience for consumer marketing and hospitality.

name: La Lorraine Bakery Group
desc: Belgian family business and the country's largest industrial bakery, producing bread and pastry products for international markets.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 513m (2012); about USD 564m at EUR 1.10
markets: Belgium's largest industrial bakery with production sites serving retail and food-service customers; export footprint not detailed.
rationale: B2B bakery supplier with limited consumer brand; F1 hospitality could support retail and food-service customer relationships.

name: Swift
desc: Member-owned co-operative running the global messaging network banks use to send cross-border payment instructions.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.114bn (2024); about USD 1.23bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Links more than 11,000 financial institutions in over 200 countries and territories.
rationale: Global payments infrastructure brand could use F1 to reach bank executives, though co-operative governance makes sponsorship spending unlikely.

name: Arla Foods
desc: Danish-Swedish farmer-owned dairy co-operative, the fifth-largest dairy company worldwide, selling Arla, Lurpak and Castello brands.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 13.8bn (2022); about USD 15.2bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells worldwide; largest dairy producer in Scandinavia and the UK, with distribution in Saudi Arabia and Indonesia.
rationale: Global dairy brands such as Lurpak target mass consumers internationally; F1's global reach suits Arla's push into Middle East and Asia.

name: Coop Danmark
desc: Danish consumer-owned grocery retailer and the country's second-largest supermarket operator with about 939 stores.
capacity_detail: Turnover DKK 46bn (2024); about USD 6.8bn at DKK 0.147
markets: Grocery retail across Denmark, running about 939 stores with 38,500 employees.
rationale: Domestic grocer with little reason to buy global F1 rights; only local race-viewing promotions would fit.

name: Danish Crown
desc: Farmer-owned Danish meat processor producing pork, beef and deli products, including the Tulip brand, for worldwide export.
capacity_detail: Turnover of approximately DKK 60bn as stated on Wikipedia; about USD 8.8bn at DKK 0.147
markets: Sells meat products worldwide from 89 production sites; owned by 5,620 Danish farmers.
rationale: Export-led food group could use F1 for B2B hospitality with global retail buyers, though consumer brand fit is weak.

name: Flying Tiger Copenhagen
desc: Danish variety store chain selling low-priced design-led homeware, gifts and toys through over 1,000 shops.
capacity_detail: Revenue DKK 5.2bn (2024); about USD 764m at DKK 0.147
markets: Present in 45 markets; European core network owned by the group, most markets outside Europe franchised.
rationale: Playful Scandinavian design retailer aimed at young shoppers; F1 merchandise collaborations could build traffic, though budgets are modest.

name: JYSK
desc: Danish retail chain selling mattresses, furniture and home décor through more than 3,400 stores in 48 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6.2bn (2025); about USD 6.8bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Stores across Europe plus Canada, Gulf states, Vietnam, Uruguay, Morocco and Central Asia.
rationale: Fast-expanding mass-market home retailer in 48 countries; F1 reach could support brand awareness in Canada, Gulf and new markets.

name: Salling Group
desc: Denmark's largest retailer, operating Netto, Føtex, Bilka and Salling stores plus Rimi in the Baltic states.
capacity_detail: Revenue DKK 83.168bn (2025); about USD 12.2bn at DKK 0.147
markets: Stores in Denmark, Germany, Poland and the Baltic states, over 2,100 locations.
rationale: Regional grocer with Netto in Germany and Poland; sponsorship would be local, so global F1 rights fit poorly.

name: Devoteam
desc: French technology consulting firm delivering cloud, data and digital transformation services with partners such as AWS and Google.
ownership: private equity: KKR (with founders Stanislas and Godefroy de Bentzmann)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.13bn (2023); about USD 1.24bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Operates in over 20 countries across Europe, the Middle East and Africa for private and public clients.
rationale: Tech consultancy competing with F1-sponsoring rivals like Cognizant and Globant; F1 tech storytelling suits its cloud and AI pitch.

name: FM Logistic
desc: French family-owned contract logistics group providing warehousing, transport and supply-chain services for retail and industry.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.86bn (2025); about USD 2.05bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Contract logistics and transport for retail and industry; country footprint not detailed on the page read.
rationale: B2B logistics brand could mirror DHL's F1 role on a smaller scale, using hospitality to win retail and FMCG contracts.

name: Groupe Atlantic
desc: French family-owned manufacturer of heat pumps, boilers, water heaters and air-conditioning equipment for homes and buildings.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.8bn (2024); about USD 3.1bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Present in more than a dozen countries with over thirty factories, thirteen of them in France.
rationale: Heat-pump maker selling energy-efficiency could link brand to F1 sustainability messaging, but its markets are mainly European.

name: Laboratoires Pierre Fabre
desc: French pharmaceutical and dermo-cosmetics group behind Avène, Klorane and Ducray, majority-owned by a public-interest foundation.
capacity_detail: Group revenues EUR 3bn in 2025; about USD 3.3bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Products sold in over 130 countries with subsidiaries founded across Europe since 1970.
rationale: Dermo-cosmetic brands like Avène sell globally to consumers; F1 skincare or sun-care tie-ins could help, as rival ELEMIS shows.

name: MACIF
desc: French mutual insurer covering motor, home, health and life risks for 5.5 million members, part of Aéma Groupe.
capacity_detail: Premium volume EUR 7.824bn in 2025; about USD 8.6bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Insurance for French households and members, mainly in France.
rationale: Domestic mutual insurer with motor insurance focus; French Grand Prix-style local activation only, global F1 rights fit poorly.

name: Murex
desc: French software company whose MX.3 platform handles trading, treasury, risk and processing for banks and asset managers.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 453m (2025); about USD 498m at EUR 1.10
markets: Serves banks worldwide including UBS, National Bank of Canada, Bank of China and OCBC; over 3,400 staff.
rationale: Fintech software vendor selling to global banks; F1 hospitality, used by rival financial-tech sponsors, could entertain bank decision makers.

name: Rothschild & Co
desc: Family-controlled financial advisory, wealth and asset management group taken private by the Rothschild family in 2023.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.9bn (2024); about USD 3.2bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Advisory, wealth and asset management from Paris and London, serving governments, corporations and private clients internationally.
rationale: Premium advisory brand courting wealthy clients and CEOs; F1 hospitality fits, and peers such as UBS and Goldman Sachs already sponsor.

name: Sagemcom
desc: French maker of broadband boxes, set-top boxes and smart energy meters supplied to telecom operators and utilities.
ownership: private equity: Charterhouse Capital Partners (70%, employees 30%)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.3bn (2024); about USD 2.5bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Present in over 50 countries through around sixty entities, including Canada, USA, Mexico, Chile, Argentina and Brazil.
rationale: B2B device maker selling to operators worldwide; F1 hospitality could entertain telecom and utility buyers, but consumer brand is limited.

name: Groupe Rocher
desc: French family-owned cosmetics group behind Yves Rocher, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Sabon and Arbonne, selling plant-based beauty products.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.2bn (2024); about USD 2.4bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells cosmetics internationally through stores, online and direct sales, with a growing share outside France.
rationale: Mass beauty brand reaching women worldwide could target F1's growing female audience, following ELEMIS and SkinCeuticals into the sport.

name: ALDI Nord
desc: German family-owned discount grocery chain operating about 6,300 stores in Europe and Trader Joe's in the US.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 31bn for Aldi Nord (2025); about USD 34.1bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Discount stores in Germany, Poland, France, Spain, Portugal, Netherlands, Belgium and more; Trader Joe's in the United States.
rationale: Huge European discounter; F1 offers mass reach but discount positioning and frugal marketing culture make a deal unlikely.

name: BEUMER Group
desc: German family-owned maker of conveyors, sortation, palletising and baggage-handling systems for airports, logistics and industry.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 1.3bn (2025); about USD 1.43bn at EUR 1.10
sponsorships: Main partner of FC Schalke 04 (per German Wikipedia)
markets: Subsidiaries in USA, Australia, South America, China, India and Europe; sells worldwide.
rationale: Engineering brand already sponsoring football (FC Schalke 04); F1 hospitality could reach airport and logistics buyers globally.

name: Boehringer Ingelheim
desc: World's largest private pharmaceutical company, developing human medicines and animal health products, owned by founding families.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 27.8bn (2025); about USD 30.6bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Operates globally with more than 54,000 employees in 76 countries.
rationale: Prescription-led pharma faces advertising limits, but animal health and employer branding could use F1's global platform modestly.

name: Bosch
desc: German engineering group making automotive parts, power tools, home appliances and industrial technology, owned by a foundation.
ownership: foundation-owned: Robert Bosch Stiftung (94%), Bosch family (5%)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 90.34bn (2024); about USD 99.4bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Global operations across automotive, industrial, consumer goods and building technology.
rationale: Leading automotive supplier with motorsport heritage; F1's new hybrid and sustainable-fuel rules suit Bosch technology and power-tool brands.

name: Brainlab
desc: German medical technology company developing software-guided surgery, radiosurgery and digital health systems for hospitals.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 429.2m (2022/23); about USD 472m at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells worldwide from 23 locations, with hospital customers internationally.
rationale: Precision-technology brand could echo F1 engineering, but hospital buyers make a sponsorship return hard to justify.

name: CHECK24
desc: German comparison portal for insurance, energy, credit, travel and products, earning commission on contracts and bookings.
capacity_detail: Group revenue EUR 500m (2015/16); about USD 550m at EUR 1.10
sponsorships: Main sponsor of ARD Sportschau 2016-2021; title sponsor of Sport1 Doppelpass 2017-2021
markets: Serves German consumers comparing insurance, energy, banking, travel and shopping offers.
rationale: Heavy sports advertiser in Germany (Sportschau, Doppelpass); domestic focus limits global F1 value, but German broadcasts fit.

name: DVAG (Deutsche Vermögensberatung)
desc: German financial advisory network selling insurance, pensions and investment products through self-employed advisers, majority family-owned.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.50bn (2022); about USD 2.75bn at EUR 1.10
sponsorships: Michael Schumacher partner since 1997; Mick Schumacher partner
markets: Advises clients mainly in Germany, with operations in Austria and other European countries.
rationale: Long-time Michael and Mick Schumacher sponsor; F1 already central to its brand, so a team deal is a natural step.

name: Dr. Oetker
desc: German family-owned food maker producing baking mixes, frozen pizza, puddings and desserts, part of the Oetker Group.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 4.2bn (2023); about USD 4.6bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Production and sales in Germany, Europe, Turkey and Tunisia, with exports to more than 15 African countries.
rationale: Mass-market frozen pizza and baking brands target families globally; F1 viewing occasions could support pizza marketing.

name: Döhler
desc: German family-owned supplier of flavours, colours, fruit preparations and beverage bases to food and drink manufacturers.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3,624.6m (2024); about USD 3.99bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Subsidiaries in India, Russia, Poland, China, Brazil, Dubai and Europe, serving beverage makers worldwide.
rationale: B2B ingredients firm with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could host beverage-industry clients, but fit is weak.

name: Emma - The Sleep Company
desc: German direct-to-consumer seller of mattresses, beds, pillows and duvets under the Emma brand worldwide.
ownership: family-owned: Franz Haniel & Cie (majority), founders hold the rest
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 766m (2025); about USD 843m at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells worldwide online and in retail, with offices in Manila, Lisbon, Shanghai and Mexico City.
rationale: Consumer sleep brand selling in many countries; F1 recovery and performance messaging fits, as Eight Sleep's team deal shows.

name: Exyte
desc: German engineering firm designing and building semiconductor, battery, life-sciences and data-centre facilities worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 6.4bn (2024); about USD 7.0bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Builds high-tech facilities worldwide, with a joint EPC brand Nixyte for Southeast Asia.
rationale: High-tech builder for chip makers could use F1 hospitality to meet semiconductor executives, but has little consumer brand need.

name: Kempinski Hotels
desc: Europe's oldest luxury hotel group, managing five-star hotels and residences across Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia.
ownership: private: majority held by sheikhs of Bahrain
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 2.9bn (2025)
markets: Operates 75 five-star hotels in 38 countries across Europe, Africa, Middle East and Asia, excluding the Americas.
rationale: Luxury hotel brand with Gulf ownership and Middle East hotels; F1's Bahrain, Abu Dhabi and Qatar races fit its guest base.

name: KiK Textilien und Non-Food
desc: German discount retailer selling low-priced clothing and household non-food goods through stores in Europe.
ownership: family-owned: Tengelmann Verwaltungs- und Beteiligungs GmbH
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.4bn (2023); about USD 2.64bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Stores in Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Italy, Romania, Bulgaria, Spain, Portugal and other European countries.
rationale: Budget fashion retailer with price-led marketing; F1's premium image fits poorly with its discount positioning.

name: Lidl
desc: German discount supermarket chain with over 12,000 stores in Europe and the US, part of the Schwarz Group.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 132.1bn (2024); about USD 145bn at EUR 1.10
sponsorships: Sponsor of the 2023 UCI Cycling World Championships in Scotland
markets: Over 12,000 stores across about 30 European countries and the United States.
rationale: Mass-market grocer that sponsors sport (2023 Cycling World Championships); F1's European audience could support awareness campaigns.

name: Pepperl+Fuchs
desc: German maker of sensors and explosion-protection components for factory and process automation.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 930m (2023), after first exceeding EUR 1bn in 2022; about USD 1.02bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells automation components internationally, with production in Germany, Asia including Vietnam, and other countries.
rationale: Sensor technology firm could showcase precision engineering, but industrial buyers give limited return on F1 rights.

name: Rhenus Logistics
desc: German logistics group providing freight, contract logistics, port and public-transport services, owned by the Rethmann Group.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 8.2bn (2025); about USD 9.0bn at EUR 1.10
markets: International logistics with 39,000 employees, including Canada, Switzerland and other countries.
rationale: Global freight and contract logistics provider; F1's logistics operation offers a natural showcase, as DHL demonstrates.

name: Rossmann
desc: German drugstore chain selling cosmetics, personal care and household goods in over 4,000 stores in Europe.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 12.15bn (2022); about USD 13.4bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Stores in Germany, Poland, Hungary, Czechia, Turkey, Albania, Kosovo, Spain and other European countries.
rationale: Large European drugstore chain; F1 hospitality fits poorly, though beauty private labels could target growing female fans.

name: Siegwerk
desc: German family-owned maker of printing inks and coatings, the world's third-largest ink producer, for packaging.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.185bn (2021); about USD 1.3bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Operates through 36 country subsidiaries, including Mexico, the Philippines and Brazil.
rationale: B2B packaging-ink maker with no consumer brand; F1 only useful for client hospitality.

name: dSPACE
desc: German developer of hardware and software for simulating and validating vehicle control units and autonomous driving systems.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 460m (2024); about USD 506m at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells development tools to automotive, aerospace and energy customers internationally.
rationale: Simulation tools used by carmakers; F1 engineering showcase could impress OEM buyers, though budget is modest.

name: ifm
desc: German family-owned maker of sensors, controllers and systems for industrial automation.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.37bn (2024); about USD 1.5bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Sales companies worldwide, with production and development in Tettnang and other sites.
rationale: Industrial sensor maker; F1 precision engineering image offers B2B hospitality value, little consumer benefit.

name: zooplus
desc: German online retailer of pet food and supplies, taken private by Hellman & Friedman and EQT in 2021.
ownership: private equity: Hellman & Friedman and EQT
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.678bn (2023); about USD 2.95bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells pet food and supplies online to customers across many European countries.
rationale: European e-commerce brand; F1 could reach affluent pet owners, but marketing is performance-led online.

name: BIP
desc: Italian consulting firm advising companies and public bodies on technology, data and transformation projects.
capacity_detail: Revenue about EUR 530m (2023); about USD 583m at EUR 1.10
markets: Headquartered in Milan and operating in 12 other countries with about 6,500 employees.
rationale: Growing consultancy competing with F1-linked rivals such as Akkodis and Cognizant; F1 hospitality could win enterprise clients.

name: Chiesi Group
desc: Italian family-controlled pharmaceutical company developing respiratory, rare-disease and specialty medicines sold in 100 nations.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3bn (2023); about USD 3.3bn at EUR 1.10
markets: 31 affiliates worldwide, about 7,200 employees, medicines provided in 100 nations.
rationale: Prescription pharma faces promotion limits; F1 would serve only corporate and employer branding.

name: Diesel
desc: Italian fashion brand known for denim, clothing and accessories, owned by Renzo Rosso's OTB Group.
ownership: founder-owned: Renzo Rosso via OTB Group
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 2.1bn (2015); about USD 2.3bn at EUR 1.10
sponsorships: Title sponsor of World Superbike in 1992 (historic)
markets: Thousands of points of sale across about eighty countries, including company-owned and franchised stores.
rationale: Provocative youth fashion brand with motorsport history (World Superbike title sponsor 1992); F1's young audience suits capsule collaborations.

name: Fidia Farmaceutici
desc: Italian pharmaceutical company specialising in hyaluronic-acid-based medicines and medical devices, owned by the Pizzocaro family holding.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 538m (2025); about USD 592m at EUR 1.10
markets: Most sales realised abroad, according to Italian Wikipedia, which says around 70% of revenue comes from exports.
rationale: Joint-care and sports-medicine products could link to athlete performance, though budgets for F1 are limited.

name: Granarolo
desc: Italian dairy group producing milk, yoghurt, cheese and plant-based drinks, controlled by the Granlatte farmers' co-operative.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.813bn (2025); about USD 1.99bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Sells dairy products in Italy and abroad after an internationalisation drive since 2011.
rationale: Italian dairy brand with export ambitions; F1's Italian fanbase suits domestic promotions more than global rights.

name: Gruppo Amadori
desc: Italian family-owned agri-food group producing chicken, processed meats, eggs and plant-based products through an integrated supply chain.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1.78bn (2023); about USD 1.96bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Operates mainly in Italy with hatcheries, feed mills, six processing plants and about 800 farms.
rationale: Domestic food brand; Italian Grand Prix activation possible, but global F1 rights exceed its mainly Italian market.

name: Impresa Pizzarotti
desc: Italian family-owned construction and civil engineering contractor building infrastructure, buildings and major projects at home and abroad.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 1,255.9m (2022); about USD 1.38bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Works in Italy and abroad since the 1970s; listed among ENR top international contractors.
rationale: B2B contractor with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could help win infrastructure bids, especially in Gulf host countries.

name: Kedrion Biopharma
desc: Italian producer of plasma-derived therapies, merged with Bio Products Laboratory and owned by Permira with an Emirati sovereign fund.
ownership: private equity: Permira (with an Emirati sovereign fund; Marcucci family and FSI minority)
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 808.8m (2019); about USD 890m at EUR 1.10
markets: Leading Italian plasma-derivatives producer and among the main producers worldwide; combined with UK-based Bio Products Laboratory.
rationale: Specialist plasma-medicines maker selling to hospitals; F1 sponsorship would offer little commercial return beyond employer branding.

name: Kerakoll
desc: Italian family-owned maker of tile adhesives, mortars, coatings and green building materials.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 706m (2024); about USD 777m at EUR 1.10
markets: Makes building materials in Sassuolo, Italy; certified B Corp; international footprint not detailed on the page read.
rationale: Building-materials brand for trade buyers; motorsport hospitality could support distributor relationships, limited consumer value.

name: Loacker
desc: South Tyrolean family-owned confectionery maker producing wafers and chocolate products sold in Italy and abroad.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 435.45m (2023); about USD 479m at EUR 1.10
markets: After Italy, the main markets are the USA, Saudi Arabia, Israel and China.
rationale: Snack brand with strong sales in Saudi Arabia, USA and China; F1 races there could boost brand awareness.

name: Savino Del Bene
desc: Italian freight forwarder organising sea, air and road transport and customs services for importers and exporters worldwide.
ownership: private: owned by Paolo Nocentini and Silvano Brandani since 2003
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 3bn (2021); about USD 3.3bn at EUR 1.10
markets: Organises transport of goods in almost every country, with strong Italy to North America trade.
rationale: Global forwarder with Italy to North America strength; F1's logistics showcase suits a challenger to DHL seeking client hospitality.

name: Sicim
desc: Italian contractor building oil, gas and water pipelines and industrial plants, founded by the Riccardi family.
capacity_detail: Turnover EUR 847.2m (2024); about USD 932m at EUR 1.10
markets: Projects in 22 countries including Canada, United States, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kazakhstan and Mozambique.
rationale: B2B pipeline contractor for energy majors; F1 hospitality could reach Middle East clients, little consumer value.

name: Sielte
desc: Italian company building and maintaining telecommunications, energy and technology networks, owned by the Turrisi family.
capacity_detail: Revenue over EUR 900m (2025); about USD 990m at EUR 1.10
markets: Works across Italy with 30 operating centres and offices abroad.
rationale: Domestic network contractor; F1 offers little benefit beyond client hospitality at Monza.

name: Sirti
desc: Italian engineering firm designing, building and maintaining telecom, transport and energy networks and digital solutions.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 743m (2022); about USD 817m at EUR 1.10
markets: Works mainly in Italy, with historic international projects such as a Persian Gulf to Red Sea cable link.
rationale: B2B network builder for telecom and energy operators; F1 would serve client hospitality rather than consumer branding.

name: Zambon
desc: Italian family-run pharmaceutical and chemicals group led by Elena Zambon, granddaughter of the founder.
capacity_detail: Revenues EUR 843m as stated on the company homepage; about USD 927m at EUR 1.10
markets: Products present in 87 countries, with sites in Europe, China, Indonesia, Brazil, Colombia and the USA.
rationale: Respiratory and consumer-health brands could gain from F1 visibility in Latin America and Asia, but budget fit is uncertain.
